en: Buddhavamsa 11.
The Lineage of the Buddha Nārada "After Paduma," [it was said].
The Fully Awakened One, supreme among bipeds,
named Narada by name,
is peerless and without equal.
Thus the Buddha, the eldest and beloved legitimate son of the Wheel-turning Monarch,
with his garlands and ornaments cast aside, [went forth].
He approached the park.
There was a tree there, vast in its glory,
beautiful, tall, and pure.
Having reached its middle,
he sat down beneath Mahāsoṇa;
there, the supreme knowledge arose.
Infinite and like a diamond;
with that, one investigates formations as being turned up and turned down.
Therein he carried away all defilements without remainder;
he attained complete enlightenment.
And having attained enlightenment through fourteen [days] of Buddha-knowledge,
he set in motion the Wheel of Dhamma.
There was the first realization for one hundred thousand times ten million [beings].
[He addressed] Mahādoṇa, the king of the nāgas.
Taming [beings], the Great Sage then performed a miracle,
displaying it to the world including the devas.
Then, during that proclamation of the Dhamma, ninety thousand times ten million gods and humans—
They crossed over all doubt at that time when the Great Hero exhorted his own son.
There was a third realization for eighty thousand times ten million;
there were three such assemblies.
Of the great seer Nārada;
there was the first assembly of one hundred thousand times ten million.
When the Buddha revealed the qualities of a Buddha along with their causal basis,
ninety thousand koṭis [of beings]—
Then the waters became pure when the Naga Verocana gave a gift to the Teacher.
Then eighty hundred thousand sons of the Conqueror assembled; at that time, I—
With matted hair and fierce asceticism,
I was a wanderer through the air,
having reached the further shore of the five super-knowledges.
Then, having satisfied with food and drink that peerless one who is equal to none, together with his Saṅgha and his retinue, I—
I honored him with sandalwood paste.
Then Nārada, the leader of the world, gave me this prophecy:
"In immeasurable eons,
this one will become a Buddha.
Having exerted himself in the supreme effort..."
"...we shall see this face-to-face.
Having heard her words as well, [he said:]...
Greatly gladdening my mind,
I resolved upon a formidable ascetic practice for the sake of fulfilling the ten perfections.
The city was named Dhaññavatī,
the kṣatriya king was named Sudeva,
and the mother was named Anomā.
Of the great seer Nārada.
He dwelt in the household life for nine thousand years;
Jita, Vijitābhirāma, and the third,
Pāsāduttama— these three supreme palaces [were built] by thirty-four thousand [craftsmen].
The women were beautifully adorned;
the woman was named Vijitasenā,
and her son was named Nanduttara.
Having seen four omens,
he went forth on foot;
for seven days he practiced the course of striving.
The Teacher, the Supreme Person,
Nārada, the leader of the world, being entreated by Brahmā, [spoke].
The Great Hero set the wheel in motion at the supreme Dhananjayā Grove;
Bhaddasāla was Jitamitta.
were his chief disciples;
the attendant of the great seer Nārada was named Vāseṭṭha.
Uttarā and Phaggunī were his two chief female disciples;
such was the Bodhi tree of that Blessed One.
He was called Mahāsoṇa.
Uggarinda and Vasabha were his chief supporters.
Indāvarī and Vaṇḍī were his chief attendants.
Eighty thousand *ratana*s—
The Great Sage has risen up high;
resembling a priceless golden ornament,
he shines throughout the ten thousand worlds.
From his body, a fathom-wide radiance streams out in every direction,
continuously by day and by night.
He always travels for a league.
At that time, there were no people at all within a league on every side.
They light up torches and lamps,
yet they are eclipsed by the rays of the Buddha.
For ninety thousand years,
As long as his life-span lasted,
for that long he remained,
delivering many people.
Just as the sky is graced by the variegated presence of owls,
so too is his teaching.
It shines with the Arahants,
and with those others who have entered the path for crossing over the stream of saṃsāra.
Having established the firm bridge of Dhamma,
that bull among men has attained Nibbāna;
he too was a Buddha, peerless and equal to the unequaled.
Those whose taints are exhausted possess incomparable splendor;
all that has vanished, for indeed,
all conditioned phenomena are empty.
Nārada, the bull among Jinas,
attained nibbāna in the city of Sudassana;
right there stands his excellent stupa.
“Rising four yojanas high.
This is the ninth lineage of the Blessed One Nārada.
